name: Grizelda Ironside
equipment: An insignia of rank (Ironside Company, mercenary regiment)
A contract of employment (escorting Scholar Dalwick to the tower ruins, now voided by dimension travel)
features: Dwarven Resilience (advantage on saves vs. poison, resistance to poison damage)
Dwarven Combat Training (proficiency with battleaxe, handaxe, light hammer, warhammer)
Dwarven Armor Training (proficiency with light and medium armor)
Stonecunning (double proficiency on History checks related to stonework)
Fighting Style: Defense (+1 AC when wearing armor, included in AC)
Second Wind (bonus action to regain 1d10+5 HP, once per short/long rest)
Action Surge (take one additional action, once per short/long rest)
Extra Attack (attack twice when taking the Attack action)
Weapon Bond (bond with up to 2 weapons, can summon bonded weapon as bonus action if on the same plane)
Spellcasting (Eldritch Knight — INT-based, abjuration and evocation focus)
War Magic (when casting a cantrip, can make one weapon attack as bonus action)
Military Rank (Soldier feature — soldiers recognize your authority and defer to you)

personality.traits: I assess every room for tactical advantages and exits before I assess its decor. I express affection through gruff insults and I express anger through gruffer insults. I am deeply suspicious of anything that doesn't obey the laws of physics, which in Wonderland means I am suspicious of everything, always.
personality.ideals: Order. The world works because things have rules. Gravity pulls down. Steel is hard. Contracts are binding. Wonderland breaks all of these rules and it makes me want to hit something — which, fortunately, is what I'm best at.
personality.bonds: I was hired to escort a scholar named Dalwick to the tower ruins where the looking glass was found. When the mirror activated and pulled us through, Dalwick vanished into Wonderland somewhere. My contract says I protect my client, and a dwarf honors her contracts. I need to find Dalwick and get us both home. Also, my warhammer has been in my family for four generations, and if Wonderland damages it I will take that very personally.
personality.flaws: I have zero imagination and I'm proud of it. Wonderland runs on imagination, which makes me spectacularly ill-suited for this place. I also refuse to accept that anything in Wonderland makes sense, even when it demonstrably does (on its own terms). I solve most problems by hitting them, and I am beginning to realize that you cannot hit a time loop or a talking doorknob. This frustrates me enormously.

appearance: A compact, powerfully built mountain dwarf standing 4'6" with arms like tree trunks and a jaw that looks like it was carved from granite. Her skin is ruddy and weathered, crisscrossed with small scars from decades of professional combat. Her iron-gray hair is worn in severe, practical braids tucked under her helm, and her beard — neatly trimmed to regulation length — is braided with small steel rings. Her eyes are slate-blue, sharp, and permanently narrowed in an expression that says 'I am not amused.' She wears immaculate plate armor over a quilted gambeson — the armor is dwarven-made, decorated with geometric patterns along the pauldrons, and maintained with obsessive care. Her shield is plain steel, dented from use, functional without ornamentation. Her warhammer — a family weapon named 'Grudgebringer' — is a masterwork piece with runes etched into the head. She moves with the measured, deliberate gait of a professional soldier who has learned that rushing gets people killed. A small hedgehog familiar named Spike sometimes peeks out from a pouch on her belt — she denies being fond of it.
backstory: Grizelda Ironside has been a professional soldier for thirty-two years, which in dwarven terms means she's barely warmed up. She served in the Ironside Company — a mercenary regiment founded by her grandmother — specializing in escort missions, dungeon clearance, and 'things that need hitting.' She is not a hero, not an adventurer, and not interested in wonder, mystery, or personal growth. She is a professional who does her job, collects her pay, and maintains her equipment. She was hired by a scholar named Aldric Dalwick to escort him to a ruined wizard's tower on the edge of civilization. Standard escort job: get the academic there alive, keep watch while he pokes at old magic, get him home. The pay was good. The contract was clear. What was NOT in the contract was being yanked through a magical looking glass into a dimension where cats disappear, tea parties last forever, and flowers have opinions. When the mirror activated, Grizelda grabbed Dalwick's arm — but the transit separated them, depositing Grizelda in one part of Wonderland and Dalwick somewhere else entirely. She doesn't know where he is, but her contract says she protects him until the job is done, and Grizelda Ironside has never broken a contract. So she will march through this ridiculous, physics-defying, logic-insulting nonsense realm, find her client, find a way home, and submit an invoice for hazard pay that will make Dalwick's grandchildren weep. The fact that Wonderland's inhabitants are suffering under a tyrant is unfortunate, and she may deal with that along the way, but it is NOT part of the original contract. She has, however, quietly bonded a second weapon in Wonderland — because Wonderland is the kind of place where you might need to summon a warhammer from across the room. She hates that she's adapting.
